ε.name: Epsilon
ε.meaning: A small quantity or a single-particle energy level; also an energy-density difference (e.g. between two vacua). Its meaning is fixed by each formula.

κ.name: Kappa
κ.meaning: A coefficient: a decay constant (how fast a wave dies inside a barrier), a curvature of a curve, or a transmission coefficient in reaction rates.

Ω.name: Capital omega (angular velocity)
Ω.meaning: Angular velocity of a rotating body (rad/s), e.g. a spinning star; elsewhere a count of microstates or a solid angle.

∂.name: Partial-derivative operator ∂
∂.meaning: The bare partial derivative operator; ∂_μ means ∂/∂x^μ, differentiating along the coordinate μ of spacetime.

τ.name: Tau
τ.meaning: Proper or worldsheet time; also a time constant or age. τ^a (a = 1,2,3) are the Pauli matrices generating weak-isospin rotations.

gY.name: Hypercharge coupling g_Y
gY.meaning: Strength of the U(1) hypercharge gauge force (often written g′); together with the weak coupling g it fixes the photon/Z mixing.

I0.name: Initial value I₀
I0.meaning: Starting value of a quantity I, e.g. the capability of a learning system or the initial intensity of a beam, at time zero.

t0.name: Initial time t₀
t0.meaning: The moment from which time is measured in a problem.

χ.name: Euler characteristic χ
χ.meaning: A whole number that a shape keeps under any stretching: vertices − edges + faces. Sphere 2, torus 0, a surface of genus g: 2 − 2g.

gs.name: String coupling g_s
gs.meaning: How strongly strings split and join; it is set by the dilaton field and controls the size of the hidden eleventh dimension.

ls.name: String length l_s
ls.meaning: The natural length of a fundamental string, l_s = √α′; the tension is 1/(2π l_s²).

l11.name: Eleven-dimensional Planck length
l11.meaning: The length at which gravity in eleven dimensions becomes strong; it fixes the 11-D gravitational coupling 2κ² = (2π)⁸ l₁₁⁹.
